name: Zipf Deviation
description: Measures deviation from Zipf's Law word distribution (Gehrmann, 2019)
mechanism:
This method performs linguistic analysis for AI-generated 文本 detection:

1. **Text Preprocessing**: The input 文本 is tokenized and processed for analysis.

2. **特征提取**: Measures deviation from Zipf's Law word distribution (Gehrmann, 2019). Relevant linguistic features are computed from the 文本.

3. **Statistical Analysis**: Features are compared against baseline distributions from human-written vs AI-generated corpora.

4. **Pattern Detection**: Anomalous patterns characteristic of AI generation are identified.

5. **分数计算**: A confidence score (0-100) is calculated based on detected patterns.
parameters:
分析类型: 统计
媒体: 文本
输入: Raw 文本 string
Minimum 文本 length: 100 characters
输出: 置信度分数 (0-100)
处理方式: Client-side NLP analysis
accuracy: 中到高 — 65-85% 独立准确率. Performance increases significantly when combined with complementary 文本 analysis methods. Results vary with 文本 length, language, and content type.
source: Statistical NLP analysis methods for AI-generated 文本 detection. Based on computational linguistics and information theory research.
useCase: Detection of AI-generated 文本 through zipf deviation analysis. This method examines specific linguistic patterns that differ between human-written and AI-generated 文本, providing complementary evidence in a multi-method analysis pipeline.
strengths:
• Fast client-side analysis with no server required
• Effective as part of a multi-method analysis pipeline
• Works across various 文本 types and genres
• Based on established linguistic research
• Complements other 统计 文本 analysis methods
limitations:
• Best used in combination with other 文本 analysis methods
• Performance varies with 文本 length (requires sufficient 文本)
• May be affected by 文本 language and writing style
• Accuracy depends on the AI model used for generation
• Human writing can occasionally trigger false positives

references.title: Powers, D. (1998). Applications and Explanations of Zipf's Law. ACL Workshop.
Manning, C.D. & Schütze, H. (1999). Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing. MIT Press.
